measurement_notes: Fixed camera and source video mapping; body/limb matrices are modified in 3D, never screen-space mesh warping.
Native dark hand/foot component centers are image observations, not recovered anatomical joint centers.
Hands at405 far side are occluded; the far-hand target is an authored continuity constraint near the visible hand.
Foot tracks after417 use explicit native ROIs and dark-component centroids; near-foot ROI excludes the connected torso shadow.
Head yaw 411..415 represents self-occlusion documented by source frame review, not a claim of recovered physical angle.

406..410 single visible foot is positive-Y; lower-right dark tail is explicitly excluded from foot targets. Native dense annotations in assets/naiwa/animation/landing_landmarks.json are the observation provenance.
Independent source feet are split at Z=-0.430 into groups16/17. Hip-knee-ankle IK retains leg segment lengths; feet rotate around connected ankles.

Ankle pivots are the measured source cut-ring centroids: (-.0567979,-.11905167,-.430) and (-.05808536,.1229324,-.430), replacing the earlier approximate ankles. The same point is enforced on calf and foot matrices.

Frames406–410 show only the near foot: far foot uses an authored point 5px right/12px above the near-foot observation and a body-surface depth upper bound, expressing reference self-occlusion. Near-foot anchors use actual winning RGB332 dark pixels, not the entire visible foot surface.
surface_anchor_method: Source-space barycentric mean of visible dark pixels in the fixed-point no-Z painter. Near-foot pixels after415 use the same x<110,y>=180 toe ROI as the reference; not anatomical joint centers.

continuity.knee_elbow_plane: Previous-frame hinge projection prevents mirrored IK branch jumps.
continuity.palm_roll: 90% preceding normal,10% desired normal; avoids camera-facing singular flips.
continuity.landing_knee: Source-segment length-preserving IK; transports the pure bending-plane vector, with knees directed inward during the landing blend. The final upper-foot track uses a consistent depth and 3D orientation.

foot_rotation_method: Source-foot dark-region principal axis constrains projected anatomical forward axis; depth and top-surface normal are authored with temporal rotation limits. Grounded feet retain source up orientation. These are inferred 3D poses, not measured 3D angles. Foot lateral axis is turned toward depth to reproduce the observed narrow side profile rather than exposing the full sole/palm-like top.
orientation_correction_method: Reference dark-mask area, center and principal axis fitted against integer projected, backface-selected, no-Z triangle painter with RGB332 corner-channel interpolation. Forearms use free twist and elbow-circle swivel with shoulder/hand anchors fixed. Feet use 3D rotation/depth adjustments and two-bone IK with shared measured ankle points. Late upper-foot motion uses one consistent 3D orientation and measured projected-axis track to prevent equivalent 3D solutions flipping the knee.

landing_foot_track.method: One consistent 3D foot orientation, rotated around the fixed camera depth axis to follow the measured image-plane foot axis; fixed depth relative to torso. Preserves natural continuity and shared ankle, avoiding multiple equivalent 3D fit solutions flipping the calf.

landing_hand_pose_prior.method: Validated previous standing-source model upper-hand pose supplies only elbow-plane and palm-orientation priors. Two-bone IK preserves the current shoulder and current hand contact exactly. Blend415..417 restores the lying palm without carrying414 upright-palm correction into the lying segment. A fixed50-degree forearm-axis roll exposes the palm across the lying segment while preserving elbow and contact points.
